newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks slide but hold at 900 support level.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks slide but hold at 900 support level.

text.p: Greek stocks slid during Monday's session but held at the support level of 900 points with industrials and construction closing with sharper losses as trading volume rose helped by block trades in blue-chips.

"It's a buyers market, you can find stocks at rock-bottom prices, valuations are completely unjustified. It is certain that a rebound is coming because the market is undervalued," said analyst Emmanuel Varsos at Investment Analysis.

"It is a good time for positioning. The investment alternatives are losing their glamour, investors may place their money at T-bills paying 11.50 percent but for how long -- rates will continue to fall. Soon rationality will return," he said.

Optimism was supported by the government's commitment to implement its austere economic policy as shown by the firm resistance to the farmers blockade and the unexpected drop of November inflation to 7.7 percent year-on-year from 8.3 percent in October, other brokers said.
The fall in inflation came soon after a 50 basis point cut in the key 12-month T-bill rate which came down to 11.50 percent in late November.
Traders said there was no downward effect by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's comments last week as the Athens bourse had not participated in recent rallies and was still underpriced.

"There is no linkage, the Athens bourse had not gone up to allow margin for a correction. But weakness in equities markets abroad could channel funds in cheap markets such as Greece. We could see sellers abroad and buyers in Greece," said a floor trader.
Farmers continued a 12-day blockade of major highways and road links protesting against Greece's austere 1997 budget and vowing to spend the Christmas holidays by the roadblocks.
They were demanding lower diesel fuel prices, cuts in the VAT tax on farm equipment, rescheduling of the debts by farm cooperatives to state banks and higher price supports especially for cotton.
Talks between the socialist government and representatives of the farmers broke down on Wednesday leading to a deadlock.
On Monday, national economy minister Yannos Papandoniou said the government would not bow to the farmers blackmail and would stick to its economic policies.

The Athens general share index closed down 0.69 percent or 6.25 points lower at 901.00 from Friday's 907.25 close after opening at 906.18. Turnover rose to 6.81 billion drachmas on volume of 3.1 million shares.
Bourse newcomer Athens Medical-Paleo Faliro was active in its trade debut, gaining 140 drachmas to close at 2,040. It went public at 1,900 drachmas a share.

Losers led gainers 115 to 70 with 26 issues unchanged on 211 traded. Banks fell 0.51 percent, industrials lost 1.26 percent with construction also dropping 1.0 percent. Small-caps slipped 0.11 percent. The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 551-569. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended down five drachmas at 4,190.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $7.02-$8.02. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted lower at 2,572-2,741 drachmas at the close. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
